title: fix(dedicated-autoscaler): handle burst tokenbucket edgecases and correct utilization reporting
author: Connor Liu
description: Motivation: We observed two related issues in Dedicated fleet autoscaling during a recent canary: 1) burst tokenbucket smoothing could temporarily under-report available burst capacity after a deploy (off-by-one refill window), causing unnecessary throttling and queuing; 2) utilization reporting in the fleet dashboard was double-counting certain short-lived allocations leading to inflated utilization numbers.  This PR fixes the tokenbucket refill window logic (corrects timestamp delta handling and removes an unintended integer truncation when computing refill tokens) and centralizes the utilization counters to a single reconciliation path to avoid duplicate increments from the allocation watcher and the heartbeat path. The change includes unit tests for edgecases (zero-length intervals, simultaneous refill+consume, and race between allocation create/delete and utilization reconciliation) and an integration canary that simulates bursty traffic across multiple priorities.  Changes in this PR: - Fix tokenbucket refill calculation (autoscaler/tokenbucket/refill.go): use monotonic time delta and float-based refill accumulation to avoid truncation on short intervals; add comments and a regression test. - Deduplicate utilization increments (allocator/reconcile.go, allocator/heartbeat.go): introduce reconcileUtilizationOnce() called from a single coordinator; add a metric for reconcile_count to help future debugging. - Add unit & integration tests (autoscaler/tokenbucket_test.go, allocator/reconcile_test.go, e2e/dedicated_burst_smoke_test.go). - Add a lightweight canary job config (deploy/canary/dedicated-burst-canary.yaml) used by CI. - Docs: short note in docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md about semantics of burst smoothing and what reconciler guarantees.  Testing: Local unit tests added; CI run (see checks) passed after a flaky integration test was stabilized. Ran a private canary in staging for 24h with synthetic traffic; results show reduced unnecessary throttles and utilization numbers inline with expected capacity models. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, roll forward to staging/Dedicated pool with canary enabled for 24h, then gradual ramp to production fleet over 48h.  Related: ENG-2147 (investigate burst throttling in canary), SUP-4123 (customer report of sudden increased queue times).
